# spec.terms.Spec { #fmrimod.spec.terms.Spec }

```python
Spec(events=(), baseline=())
```

An ordered collection of event and baseline terms.

Use the ``+`` operator to compose:

>>> spec = hrf("trial_type") + drift("cosine", cutoff=128) + intercept()

The container distinguishes *event* terms (HrfTerm, parametric variants)
from *baseline* terms (Drift, Intercept, Confounds). Composition routes
each term to the correct bucket automatically.

## Attributes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `terms` | All terms, events then baseline, in declaration order. |

| Name | Description |

| [diff](#fmrimod.spec.terms.Spec.diff) | Return a structural `SpecDiff` against ``other``. |

### diff { #fmrimod.spec.terms.Spec.diff }

```python
diff(other)
```

Return a structural `SpecDiff` against ``other``.

Pure equality (``self == other``) only answers yes/no; this
helper reports *what* changed: added/removed/changed terms and
the specific fields that diverge on each changed term. See
`fmrimod.spec.diff.spec_diff` for the matching rules.

### from_dict { #fmrimod.spec.terms.Spec.from_dict }

```python
from_dict(payload)
```

Reconstruct a `Spec` from `to_dict` output.

### to_dict { #fmrimod.spec.terms.Spec.to_dict }

```python
to_dict()
```

Serialize this `Spec` to a JSON-safe dict.

The inverse of `from_dict`. See
`fmrimod.spec.serialize` for the supported value set and
the explicit-error behavior on shapes that don't round-trip
(e.g. inline callables, DataFrame payloads).
